close-up-shot.context: A viewfinder frame almost filled by a head and shoulders. Used for camera shot types in film and video guides, shot lists, storyboards and editing tools.

extreme-close-up-shot.context: A viewfinder frame filled edge to edge by a single eye. Marks the extreme close-up shot in film terminology, storyboards and cinematography lessons.

wide-shot.context: A viewfinder frame with a small standing figure above a ground line and plenty of space around it. Used for wide or long shot labels in shot lists, film lessons and camera guides.

medium-shot.context: A viewfinder frame showing a figure from the waist up. Used for the medium shot in film guides, storyboards, shot lists and video editing tools.

two-shot.context: A viewfinder frame holding two people from the waist up, side by side. Used for the two shot in film and TV guides, storyboards and shot lists.

over-the-shoulder-shot.context: A viewfinder frame with the back of a large head and shoulder in one corner facing a smaller figure. Used for the over the shoulder shot in dialogue scenes, film lessons and storyboards.

point-of-view-shot.context: An eye beside a viewfinder frame that shows two arms reaching forward. Used for point of view and first person shots in film guides, games, storyboards and video tools.

dutch-angle.context: A viewfinder frame with a building and a horizon line tilted on a steep diagonal. Used for the Dutch angle or canted camera shot in film lessons, storyboards and editing tools.

overhead-shot.context: A viewfinder frame looking straight down at the top of a head and shoulders. Used for the overhead, top down or birds eye shot in film guides, storyboards and shot lists.

dolly-zoom.context: Nested viewfinder frames joined by diagonal lines, like looking down a tunnel. Stands for the dolly zoom or vertigo effect in film lessons, effects guides and camera move lists.

tracking-shot.context: A camera on a wheeled dolly rolling behind a walking figure. Used for tracking, following and dolly shots in film guides, camera move lists and storyboards.

establishing-shot.context: A wide viewfinder frame showing a row of tall buildings with a small title bar in one corner. Used for the establishing shot that opens a scene in film guides and storyboards.

panning-shot.context: A viewfinder frame with a sharp car in the middle and speed streaks behind it. Used for the panning shot that follows fast movement, in film lessons, storyboards and camera guides.

razor-edit-tool.context: A razor blade above a timeline clip that has a cut line running through it. Used for the blade or razor tool in video and audio editors to split a clip.

trim-clip.context: A timeline clip with a square bracket gripping its start edge. Used for trimming, ripple trim and in point or out point controls in video and audio editors.

dissolve-transition.context: Two overlapping clip rectangles with crossing lines where they overlap. Marks a cross dissolve or crossfade between clips in video editors and slide tools.

wipe-transition.context: A frame split by a diagonal edge, one side solid, with a small arrow moving across the edge. Marks the wipe transition between clips in video editors and slideshow tools.

fade-to-black.context: A row of three frames going from empty to half filled to solid. Stands for fading a video out to black or fading in from black in editors and playback tools.

render-queue.context: A stack of video frames with a progress bar running beneath. Used for batch rendering and export queues in video, animation and 3D software.

timeline-marker.context: A timeline ruler with a pentagon marker hanging from it and a thin line dropping from the marker. Used for markers, flags, cue points and chapters on editing timelines.

motion-tracking.context: A corner bracket target around a dot with a trail of smaller dots behind it. Used for point tracking and motion tracking tools in video effects and compositing software.

lut-cube.context: An isometric cube with one face shaded. Stands for a 3D lookup table (LUT) used for colour grading and colour conversion in video and photo tools.

vectorscope.context: A round scope display with six small target boxes around the ring and a trace in the centre. Used for the vectorscope colour monitor in video editing and colour correction tools.

title-safe-area.context: A screen with corner guides set inside its edge and two short lines of text in the middle. Marks the title safe or action safe area guides in video editors and broadcast graphics.

letterboxed-video.context: A screen with solid bars across the top and bottom and a play mark in the middle. Stands for letterbox, widescreen and cinematic aspect ratio settings in video players and editors.

zebra-stripes-warning.context: A viewfinder frame with diagonal stripes over a bright patch and a bright dot. Stands for the zebra exposure warning on cameras and video monitors that flags overexposed areas.

4k-video.context: A screen outline with the characters 4K inside it. Marks 4K ultra high definition video, resolution settings, streaming quality and export presets.

auto-reframe.context: A wide frame with a tall crop frame centred on a person inside it. Stands for automatic reframing of video to vertical or square formats around the subject.

scene-detection.context: A film strip with a cut line down its middle and a sparkle above the cut. Used for automatic scene detection and shot boundary tools that split footage into scenes.

theater-box-seat.context: A balcony box with a draped swag above and two people leaning over the rail. Used for opera and theatre box seats, balcony tickets and seating plans.

ghost-light.context: A bare light bulb in a cage on a tall stand with a tripod foot. The ghost light left burning on an empty stage, used for theatre tradition, venue pages and stage safety.

stage-flat.context: The back of a rectangular scenery panel showing its wooden frame rail and a diagonal brace. Used for set building, scenic carpentry and theatre production tools.

stage-fly-system.context: A pulley with a rope running down to a hanging scenery batten and a counterweight on the other side. Used for stage rigging, fly loft and scenery lift tools.

revolving-stage.context: A round turntable stage platform in perspective with a curved arrow above it showing rotation. Used for rotating stages, quick scene changes and theatre machinery.

theater-in-the-round.context: A top down view of a small round stage surrounded by rings of curved seating broken by aisles. Used for arena staging, circular theatres and seating plans.

wig-head.context: A mannequin head on a short stand wearing a full curly wig. Used for wig shops, costume and hair departments, theatre wardrobe and hairpiece care.

costume-rack.context: A rolling clothes rail on wheels with two costumes hanging from it. Used for wardrobe departments, theatre and film costume stock, and garment rails.

spike-mark.context: A stage floor seen from above with a T shaped tape mark and a footprint beside it. Used for blocking, actor positions and furniture marks on stage.

surtitle-screen.context: A wide narrow text screen hung on two cables above a stage opening with two short lines of text. Used for surtitles, supertitles and captions at opera and theatre.

thunder-sheet.context: A large thin metal sheet hanging from a bar with wobble lines on it and a lightning bolt beside it. Used for theatre sound effects, foley and storm sounds.

wind-machine.context: A slatted drum on a stand with a crank handle at its side. Used for theatre wind sound effects, foley and live sound effect props.

vaudeville-hook.context: A long cane with a large curved hook reaching out from the edge of a curtain. Used for vaudeville, talent shows, comedy gags and pulling an act off stage.

stagebox.context: A metal box with a grid of round connector sockets on its face and a thick cable leaving one side. Used for stage boxes, audio snakes and patch panels in live sound.

in-ear-monitor.context: An ear outline with a moulded earpiece in it and a thin cable trailing away. Used for in-ear monitors, stage monitoring and musician earphones.

line-array-speaker.context: A fan shaped stack of speaker boxes hanging from a rigging bar. Used for concert sound systems, PA rigs and flown speaker arrays.

confetti-cannon.context: A handheld tube cannon angled upward bursting a spray of small confetti pieces. Used for celebration effects, party launchers, weddings and stage finales.

stage-pyrotechnics.context: A row of small floor boxes along a stage edge each shooting a tall column of flame. Used for concert fire effects, flame projectors and live show special effects.

projection-mapping.context: A building facade with a projector beam coming in from the side and a window pattern painted across it. Used for video mapping, facade projection and light shows.

hologram-display.context: A round base sending light lines upward around a small floating figure. Used for hologram displays, 3D projection and futuristic or sci-fi interface features.

mic-flag.context: A handheld microphone with a square flag fitted around its shaft below the grille. Used for broadcast and news microphones with a station cube or logo flag.

cue-light.context: A small box on a stand with one lamp lit and a push button below it. Used for stage manager cue lights, go signals and backstage show control.

news-helicopter.context: A helicopter in side view with a round camera ball hung under its nose. Used for live aerial news, traffic reports and aerial camera coverage.

telestrator.context: A television screen showing a ringed player with a hand drawn curved arrow beside it. Used for sports analysis, screen drawing and broadcast graphics tools.

field-reporter.context: A person holding a handheld microphone, framed by a camera viewfinder. Used for news reporters, live reports, on location interviews and journalism.

film-can.context: A round flat film tin seen from above at an angle, with its lid ring and a strip of film curling out. Used for film storage, archives, cinema reels and movie distribution.

jog-shuttle-wheel.context: A round editing controller with an outer ring around an inner dimpled jog wheel. Used for jog and shuttle controls, scrubbing and playback dials in editing tools.

intertitle-card.context: An ornate rectangular frame with decorative corners and two centred lines of text. Used for silent film title cards, dialogue cards and vintage movie captions.

director-viewfinder.context: A handheld viewfinder tube with a small eyepiece, a lens ring and a neck cord hanging below. Used for the directors finder in location scouting, framing and cinematography.

shot-list.context: A clipboard with three rows, each starting with a small camera mark. Used for shot lists, shooting schedules, call sheets and camera setup planning.

animation-cel.context: A clear sheet with peg holes along the top edge and a painted character on it. Used for traditional cel animation, animator tools and frame by frame drawing.

kinetoscope.context: A tall cabinet with a peephole viewer on top and a hand crank on its side. Used for early cinema history, peep show film viewers and vintage movie machines.

onion-skinning.context: A solid ball with two faded dashed copies trailing behind it. Used for the onion skin overlay in animation software that shows previous and next frames.

tweening.context: Two solid key poses of a ball at either end with smaller in-between balls along the arc. Used for tweening, in-betweening and keyframe interpolation in animation tools.

bouncing-ball-animation.context: A ball squashed flat on a ground line with a trail of smaller balls rising away along an arc. Used for squash and stretch, the classic bouncing ball exercise and animation principles.

character-rig.context: A stick figure skeleton of straight bones joined by round joint dots. Used for character rigging, armatures, bones and inverse kinematics in 3D and 2D animation.

lip-sync-chart.context: A grid of six small mouth shapes, each open a different amount. Used for phoneme and viseme charts, dialogue animation and lip sync tools.

phenakistoscope.context: A slotted disc with a ring of slots near its rim and a short handle below it. Used for early animation history, optical toys and persistence of vision lessons.

walk-cycle.context: A row of three small figures showing the stages of a walking step. Used for walk cycles, key poses and gait in character animation and game art.

rotoscoping.context: A dashed outline traced around a head and shoulders with small square anchor points on it. Used for rotoscoping, masking and tracing footage frame by frame.

dubbing.context: A studio microphone on a stand facing a screen that shows a speaking face. Used for voice over, dubbed audio, ADR, translation and lip sync recording.

talk-show-set.context: A host desk on the left and a two seat sofa on the right in front of a city skyline backdrop. Used for chat show, late night and TV interview studio sets.

film-rewinder.context: A film reel on a spindle with a hand crank and a curved arrow showing the winding direction. Used for rewinding film, editing benches and projectionist tools.

film-trim-bin.context: A canvas bin below a pin rack with strips of film hanging down into it. Used for film editing, cutting rooms and storing trims and off cuts.
